question: Can I walk to the petroglyphs at Kejimkujik on my own as a member of the general public?
generated_answer:
Yes, you can walk to the petroglyphs at Kejimkujik on your own. However, it's important to note that the petroglyphs are located in a remote area of the park and the trails can be challenging. It's recommended to bring plenty of water, wear appropriate hiking gear, and be prepared for changing weather conditions. Additionally, visitors are asked to respect the site and not touch or damage the petroglyphs. 

If you're not comfortable with the hike or want more information, guided tours are available during the summer months. These tours provide a deeper understanding of the petroglyphs' history and significance. 

For the most up-to-date information and to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience, it's always a good idea to check with park staff or visit the park's website before heading out. 

Here is a link to the park's website for more information: [Kejimkujik National Park and National Historic Site](https://www.pc.gc.ca/en/pn-np/ns/kejimkujik) 

And here is a link to the park's visitor guide, which includes information on trails and guided tours: [Kejimkujik Visitor Guide](https://www.pc.gc.ca/en/pn-np/ns/kejimkujik/visit) 

Remember to follow all park rules and regulations to help preserve this important cultural and natural site for future generations. 

If you have any other questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask! 

Best of luck with your visit to Kejimkujik!
